title: Ameresco Reports Third Quarter 2026 Financial Results
body_markdown:
FRAMINGHAM, MA – November 9, 2026 – Ameresco, Inc. (NYSE:AMRC), a leading energy infrastructure company, today announced financial results for the third quarter ended September 30, 2026. The Company also furnished supplemental information in conjunction with this press release in a Current Report on Form 8-K. The supplemental information, which includes Non-GAAP financial measures, has been posted to the “Investors” section of the Company’s website at www.ameresco.com. Reconciliations of Non-GAAP measures to the appropriate GAAP measures are included herein. All financial result comparisons made are against the prior year period unless otherwise noted.


“Our third quarter results represented another quarter of strong growth and disciplined execution. We achieved revenue increases across each of our major business lines, expanded margins and continued to build both awarded and contracted backlogs. The $875 million in new projects we were awarded in the third quarter brought Ameresco’s total project backlog to a record $7.2 billion. This also was an excellent quarter for project contract conversion with $737 million converting from awarded into contracted backlog, building visibility as we head into 2027,” CEO George Sakellaris commented.


“The strength of our business model is reflected in the diversity of our solutions, markets and customers. We secured over $675 million in additional awards driven by strength in Federal infrastructure and Europe. We also added data center energy infrastructure awards of $200 million representing an expanded scope of work for Ameresco at an existing project. In addition, our recurring O&M and Energy Asset businesses continue to grow at an impressive pace, further enhancing long-term revenue visibility and reinforcing the resilience of our business model,” Mr. Sakellaris concluded.

(1) During Q3 2026, we changed our method of accounting for nonrefundable, transferable investment tax credits associated with our energy assets effective January 1, 2026. Under the new method, we recognize ITCs in the income tax provision in the period the credits are generated rather than as a reduction in the cost basis of the related energy assets. The change was applied retrospectively, including to our 2025 results.


(2) Net Income (loss) represents net income (loss) before non-controlling interests.


(3) Adjusted EBITDA is based on consolidated net income and no longer includes an adjustment to remove the non-controlling interest portion.


(4) Numbers in table may not sum due to rounding.


Total revenue increased 10% to $580.3 million, reflecting broad-based growth across Projects, Energy Assets and O&M and continued strong execution on project backlog conversion. Project revenue increased 9% to $446.0 million, while Energy Asset revenue grew 21% to $75.4 million, as we continued to expand our portfolio of owned operating assets. O&M revenue increased 20% to $37.0 million, driven by the continued addition of new long-term operations and maintenance contracts. Gross margin expanded to 18.7%, with meaningful improvement on both a sequential and year-over-year basis. Margin improvement was driven by a combination of a favorable business mix, strong execution and a decrease in depreciation related to an adjustment to our energy assets’ useful lives.


Net income attributable to common shareholders was $31.9 million, or $0.59 per diluted share, while Non-GAAP EPS was $0.88. Adjusted EBITDA increased 24% to $91.7 million. In Q3 we adopted HLBV accounting related to the Neogenyx Fuels transaction. HLBV accounting allocates income or loss among partners based on the change in the amounts each partner would receive if the entity were hypothetically liquidated at book value at each reporting date. This method is commonly used in tax equity and complex partnership structures. Given the inherent variability within the HLBV calculation quarter-to-quarter, to facilitate comparability, our Non-GAAP EPS and adjusted EBITDA now reflect 100% of the operating results of our consolidated joint ventures, most notably Ameresco Sunel Energy (“AMRC Sunel JV”), a significant part of our Europe segment, and Neogenyx Fuels, which constitutes substantially all of the business reported in our Renewable Fuels segment. Results of these joint ventures are included in the Non-GAAP Financial Measures below.


Earnings for the quarter also included a large tax benefit related to our planned adoption of a tax-based accounting policy as discussed last quarter. This better aligns earnings recognition with the period in which investment tax credits are generated, rather than allocating the benefit over the life of the related assets.

Unrestricted cash increased to $128.5 million with total corporate debt of $380.4 million. Our corporate leverage was 2.9x, comfortably below our 3.5x covenant. We also strengthened our capital position in Q3, securing $106 million of financing and financing commitments.


Adjusted Cash from Operations was positive in Q3. On a rolling eight-quarter basis, Adjusted Cash from Operations was approximately $26 million, compared with $30 million last quarter, primarily reflecting the timing and mix of activity in the period.

**Summary and Outlook**


“Our rapidly growing project backlog together with the strength of our recurring revenue businesses position us for continued growth in 2027 and beyond. Ameresco remains well positioned to benefit from the emerging power infrastructure opportunities within the data center and C&I landscape, while we continue to see positive trends in our traditional markets serving the federal government, municipalities, universities, schools, and hospitals. We are also at the forefront of the technology curve as we integrate fuel cells, microgrids, small and micro nuclear reactors and other cutting-edge technologies into our comprehensive portfolio of solutions helping us to meet growing industry demand,” concluded CEO George Sakellaris.

**About Ameresco, Inc.**


Ameresco, Inc. (NYSE: AMRC) is a leading energy infrastructure company delivering integrated solutions to create reliable power and modernize infrastructure. The company’s Power Infrastructure business integrates energy resources across behind-the-meter and utility-scale systems. Its Buildings & Public Infrastructure business modernizes the built environment with smart, connected solutions that optimize performance and enhance resilience. Ameresco is a trusted full lifecycle partner, delivering over $15 billion in solutions and contracting over 5 GW of energy resources since its founding in 2000. Headquartered in Massachusetts, Ameresco serves public and private sector customers across North America and Europe. Learn more at www.ameresco.com.
